chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام.

That a man caused ifda' to a woman, so she was appraised at the value of a sound female slave and at her value as one made mufda', then the difference between the two was considered and made part of her diyah, and the husband was compelled to keep her.

key_terms.أَفْضَى: caused ifda', a severe bodily injury producing a legal liability
key_terms.الزَّوْجَ: the husband, upon whom a legal obligation is imposed here
key_terms.الصَّحِيحَةِ: sound or uninjured in bodily condition
key_terms.الْأَمَةِ: the female slave, used here as the basis of valuation in the ruling
key_terms.دِيَتِهَا: her diyah, the financial compensation due for the injury
key_terms.قِيمَةَ: the assessed monetary value used for legal compensation
key_terms.مُفْضَاةً: a woman affected by ifda', i.e., in the injured state relevant to the ruling

ai.seo_question: How is compensation determined in Shia fiqh when a woman is injured by ifda'?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning injury to a woman resulting in ifda'. It states that compensation is determined by assessing the difference in value between her sound state and her injured state, and it also rules that the husband is compelled to retain her.
